---
title: "1 Theory-based methods research"
link-citations: true
---

## Definition and features
In theory-based methods research, researchers use tightly applied theory, such as mathematical derivation, proof, logic, philosophy of science, or specific theoretical frameworks, to answer a methods research question.

- Strengths include in-depth exploration of the structure, assumptions, and implications of methods.
- Limitations include unclear performance in practice.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related types
[Informal approaches](15informal.qmd): While theory-based methods research uses theory to answer a methods research question, informal approaches use theory for explanation.
:::

## Typical objectives and corresponding examples
[Propose a new method](../objectives/6propose-method.qmd): deriving a prediction interval for random effects meta-analyses;[@Higgins2009a] inverse odds weighting to operationalize transportability;[@Westreich2017transportability] adopting implementation science to the context of research methods;[@King2019using] framework to integrate external validity in deductive causal inference.[@Esterling2025the]

[Develop guidance for understanding and applying methods](../objectives/9guidance-applying.qmd): covariate adjustment in trials;[@VanLancker2024covariate] credibility criteria for observed subgroup effects.[@Schandelmaier2020development]
